acceptedAnswer.text: Manufacturing recruitment automation uses AI-assisted workflows to run repeatable industrial hiring steps — intake across plants, shift-preference surveys, certification flags, and interview scheduling — while recruiters decide who advances. For Indian factories and staffing partners, it reduces time spent chasing mismatched shift or location fits during ramp-ups and seasonal peaks.

mainEntity.name: Can AI handle multiple plant locations?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, when workflows are configured per site. Each plant can keep its own shift patterns, certification rules, and hiring manager calendars while sharing common messaging and compliance standards. The system routes candidates to the right location, avoids duplicate outreach, and alerts recruiters when one applicant qualifies for roles at more than one facility.

mainEntity.name: Do I need an ATS to use these workflows?

acceptedAnswer.text: A candidate database helps, but the core need is a workflow engine that reacts to manufacturing events — shift changes, new headcount, certification gaps. Many ATS products include workflow modules. EarlyJobs can complement your stack by coordinating outreach and handoffs; the important part is logic built around plant-specific hiring steps.

acceptedAnswer.text: Pricing depends on hiring volume, number of plants, and which workflow steps you automate. EarlyJobs typically scopes automation alongside recruitment support rather than a one-size calculator.
